questions.title: In which country outside Iran, if any, will US forces strike Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026?
questions.background: Iran-aligned armed groups operate across several Middle Eastern countries, creating potential flashpoints for military confrontation with the United States.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera, supported where available by official military statements. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country outside Iran where US forces conduct strikes against Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026, inclusive. Direct US participation in either unilateral or joint strikes qualifies; threats, proposed operations, and diplomatic support do not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name, or “None” if no qualifying strikes occur.

Crucially, after a third Saudi vessel (NCC MASA) suffered minor hull damage in a Red Sea attack on July 24—crossing Trump's July 23 red line—it was the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen (NOT the US) that launched retaliatory airstrikes on Hodeidah telecom facilities and Kamaran Island late Friday. Meanwhile, five explosive-laden drones targeted US forces near Erbil airport in northern Iraq on July 24 (shot down by US-led forces), nudging Iraq up 0.09 -> 0.11; Lebanon and Syria hold at 0.01 each.

questions.title: Which country will announce a new multinational maritime coalition to protect navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden by August 1, 2026?
questions.background: Attacks on commercial shipping since 2023 have heightened concerns about the security of maritime trade routes through the Red Sea.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country that announces the creation of a new multinational maritime coalition between July 1 and August 1, 2026, inclusive, with a stated purpose of protecting freedom of navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden. Joining an existing coalition does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-24 update (Anadolu, Al Jazeera, Voice of Emirates, UAE MOFA, SABA, African Union): No new Red Sea/Bab al-Mandeb/Gulf of Aden multinational maritime coalition has been announced yet with 8 days left until August 1, but July 23-24 developments further consolidate Saudi Arabia as the prime candidate to announce one. Conversely, France's Foreign Ministry explicitly stated on July 23 that it is protecting Red Sea navigation through existing EU Operation ASPIDES (joining/continuing an existing mission does not qualify), trimming France 0.05 -> 0.03. Lifting Saudi Arabia 0.48 -> 0.53 and edging down Egypt (0.16 -> 0.15), United States (0.10 -> 0.09, already leads Prosperity Guardian and focused on Iran/Hormuz), and United Kingdom (0.05 -> 0.04), keeping sum = 0.84 with 0.16 residual for UAE, India, Djibouti, Italy, Greece, or others.

questions.title: Who will succeed Brendon McCullum as permanent head coach of England's men's Test team?
questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution : Resolve to the first person formally appointed as McCullum's permanent successor as head coach of England's men's Test team. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-17 update: frontrunner Andy Flower publicly and formally ruled himself out of the England Test head coach race at London Spirit's media day (BBC Sport, Sky Sports, Reuters, ESPNcricinfo, Hindustan Times), confirming he turned down the ECB even with dual-role IPL flexibility because IPL/RCB duties clash with the early English summer. Following Flower's withdrawal, iNews Cricket Correspondent Chris Stocks reports on July 17 that the ECB is now pivoting to former Australia coach Justin Langer as its top target (rated 4/5; strong Ashes rebuilding pedigree and county familiarity, though tempered by LSG IPL ties and past intensity concerns), lifting Langer 0.13 -> 0.26. Newly available Stephen Fleming (co-rated 4/5 by iNews, named by BBC Sport July 17) rises 0.19 -> 0.25 as he just left CSK after 18 years—removing the IPL clash that deterred Flower—was Rob Key's 2022 preference, and publicly welcomed an approach this week. Among remaining shortlisted contenders, Jonathan Trott (0.15 -> 0.16, English, available, named by BBC Sport/iNews 3/5), Richard Dawson (0.07 -> 0.09, English, ECB pathway, named by BBC Sport July 17), and Tom Moody (new entry at 0.07, explicitly named by BBC Sport July 17 alongside Trott, Dawson, and Fleming) round out the top 5, leaving 17% residual for Kumar Sangakkara, Mike Hesson, Adi Birrell, and unlisted options as BBC notes the ECB is still in an initial stage and open to an interim for August's Pakistan series.

questions.title: Which Federal Reserve policymakers will vote for an interest-rate increase at the July 29, 2026 FOMC meeting?
questions.background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one. Accepted Answer Format : All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will announce a finalized voluntary repatriation plan for thousands of Myanmar refugees in August 2026?
questions.background: Repatriation means returning refugees to their country of origin. This question concerns finalization of a government plan, rather than the completion of refugee returns.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or reliable news reporting directly quoting those statements. Resolving Event : During August 2026, a Southeast Asian government publicly confirms that it has finalized a voluntary repatriation programme, or the first phase of such a programme, covering at least 1,000 refugees from Myanmar. A preliminary agreement to consider returns is insufficient. Actual departures need not have occurred. Accepted Answer Format : The common English name of the country finalizing the repatriation plan, not the destination country.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-22 local breaking update (AFP via Straits Times, July 22): Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow confirmed on July 21 that Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing will meet Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Bangkok on August 6-7, 2026—directly inside the August 2026 window—following Thailand's July 12 Bangkok ASEAN-Myanmar ministerial talks. Thailand is pursuing an explicit 'dual-track approach' with Naypyidaw on pressing bilateral border issues, already hosts ~80,155 registered Myanmar border-camp refugees under a May-June 2026 camp-closure timeline, and has established UNHCR voluntary-return mechanisms. Conversely, while Malaysia hosts >215,000 UNHCR refugees (>126,000 Rohingya) amid surging domestic anti-Rohingya pressure (July 21 AFP/Straits Times) and engaged Myanmar's FM in May-June, practical Rohingya voluntary repatriation to Arakan Army-contested Rakhine State faces severe barriers (underscored by ~500 Rohingya feared dead in July boat sinkings fleeing Rakhine) and Malaysia has no scheduled August leaders' summit with Min Aung Hlaing. Lifting Thailand 0.52 -> 0.65, trimming Malaysia 0.39 -> 0.28 and Indonesia 0.06 -> 0.04, and keeping Laos (0.01) and Cambodia (0.01) with 1% residual.
